hero.lead: An archipelago of 116.8 million where the World Bank committed $1 billion for energy and water security and $600 million for 21 million students in 2026.

stats.label: Students in a new learning programme

capital.heading: The Philippines borrows on its reforms, and the world lends. Next, every child reading by ten.

record.text: Total outstanding national government debt at end-June 2026: domestic debt P12.84 trillion (67.33%), external debt P6.23 trillion (32.67%)
ADB crisis financing through the Countercyclical Support Facility, approved 24 September 2026, to protect families from rising prices
Second Energy Transition and Climate Resilience Development Policy Loan: $1 billion IBRD loan and a $20 million grant, approved June 2026
Sustainable Agricultural Transformation, a results-based programme for at least five million farmers, approved March 2026
Learning Upgrade Support and Decentralization (PLUS-D): reading and mathematics for 21 million learners, approved April 2026

register.name: Retail Treasury Bonds, Tranche 32 (RTB-32)
register.detail: Rate-setting auction 29 September 2026 · 6.875% a year · 2½ years · Offer 29 September to 7 October 2026 · Issue date 12 October 2026
register.note: Awarded at the rate-setting auction; the final total is not yet on a Treasury page
register.text: Peso bonds sold by the Bureau of the Treasury to Filipino savers and institutions, at 6.875% a year for two and a half years. The rate-setting auction awarded PHP 84.87 billion before the offer opened to retail investors.

register.name: US dollar global bonds, 5.5-year, 10-year and tap of 2051
register.detail: Priced 17 June 2026 · $550 million 5.5-year at 4.699% · $1.65 billion 10-year at 5.355% · $300 million tap of the 2051 bonds at 5.850% · Settlement 24 June 2026
register.note: Upsized from $2.0 billion; 4.4 times oversubscribed
register.text: A three-tranche dollar bond, upsized from $2.0 billion to $2.5 billion after the order book reached 4.4 times the amount. The Republic is using the proceeds for general budget financing.

register.name: US dollar global bonds, 5.5-year, 10-year and 25-year
register.detail: Priced 21 January 2026 · 5.5-year at Treasuries plus 50 basis points · 10-year at Treasuries plus 80 basis points · 25-year at 5.750% · Settlement 27 January 2026
register.note: Equivalent to $2.75 billion; tranche sizes not stated in the release
register.text: A three-tranche dollar bond equivalent to $2.75 billion. The proceeds are for the general purposes of the Republic, including budgetary support.

register.name: Philippines Accelerated Water and Sanitation Project in Selected Areas (AWSPSA)
register.detail: Approved 31 July 2026 · Total project cost $268.62 million · World Bank $250.87 million
register.note: Of which $250.87 million from the World Bank; the rest from the Government and private-sector equity
register.text: A World Bank Group project to expand resilient water and sanitation services on Bohol, Siargao and Jolo, areas the release calls vulnerable. It serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Second Energy Transition and Climate Resilience Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved 25 June 2026 · $1 billion IBRD loan · $20 million performance-based grant from the Livable Planet Fund
register.note: $1 billion IBRD loan and a $20 million grant
register.text: Budget support for reforms that make the renewable energy market fully operational, plan electric vehicle charging and launch a first offshore wind auction, and for cost-recovery water tariffs and bulk water pricing rules. It continues the $800 million operation of March 2025 and serves the energy and water standards.

register.name: Project for Learning Upgrade Support and Decentralization (PLUS-D)
register.detail: Approved 3 April 2026 · Kindergarten to Grade 10 and the Alternative Learning System
register.note: Reading and mathematics for 21 million learners
register.text: Raises reading and mathematics in public schools from kindergarten to Grade 10 and in the Alternative Learning System, for 21 million learners. It is aimed at the education standard, which sets Coverage for the Philippines.

register.name: Philippines Sustainable Agricultural Transformation Project (PSAT)
register.detail: Approved 27 March 2026 · Program-for-Results
register.note: At least five million farmers
register.text: A results-based programme for the agriculture sector, with funds released as agreed results are achieved. At least five million farmers are expected to benefit, which serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Philippines Growth and Jobs Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved 12 March 2026 · Development policy loan
register.note: Fiscal, investment and skills reforms
register.text: Budget support for revenue and spending reforms, private investment and innovation, and reforms in skills, education and innovation. Skills and a stronger fiscal base serve the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: First Energy Transition and Climate Resilience Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2025 · Development policy loan
register.note: Clean energy, electricity markets and water management
register.text: Budget support for reforms that scale up clean energy technologies, make electricity markets more secure, flexible and competitive, and improve water management. The $1 billion loan of June 2026 continues the series.

register.name: Assistance for Greater Resilience and Alleviation of Poverty program
register.detail: Approved 24 September 2026 · Countercyclical Support Facility · Finances the Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport
register.note: Crisis financing to protect families from rising prices
register.text: ADB crisis financing to help the Philippines protect families from rising prices. It supports fuel supplies, affordable power and health services, food and medicine costs, income support, and the return of affected overseas Filipino workers, so that the food, energy, health and livelihood standards hold through a price shock.

register.name: Marine Ecosystems for Blue Economy Development Program, subprogram 1
register.detail: Approved 11 December 2025 · Policy-based loan · AFD and KfW to cofinance up to €200 million each
register.note: Ocean and coastal reforms
register.text: Supports reforms for the sustainable management of the Philippines’ ocean ecosystems and a climate-resilient, low-carbon blue economy. Healthy coasts and fisheries serve the food and livelihood standards for coastal families.

register.name: Business Environment Strengthening with Technology Program (BEST), subprogram 1
register.detail: Approved 10 December 2025 · Policy-based loan
register.note: Faster permits and digital services for business
register.text: Supports reforms that streamline regulatory requirements for businesses, speed up permits and licences, and deliver government services to businesses online, with a database of business regulations. A simpler business climate serves the livelihood standard through private jobs.

register.name: Reducing Food Insecurity and Undernutrition with Electronic Vouchers Project
register.detail: Approved 13 August 2025 · Supports the Walang Gutom (Zero Hunger) Food Stamp Program · Cofinanced by AFD (€200 million) and the OPEC Fund ($150 million)
register.note: Electronic food vouchers for 750,000 food-insecure households
register.text: Expands the Walang Gutom (Zero Hunger) Food Stamp Program, which gives electronic food vouchers to food-insecure households across the country. It finances the food standard directly.

register.name: Malolos–Clark Railway Project, tranche 2
register.detail: Approved 16 April 2025 · Second and final tranche of a multitranche financing facility · Tranche 1, $1.3 billion, 2019
register.note: 53.1 km of the 163-km North–South Commuter Railway
register.text: Finances the 53.1-kilometre Malolos–Clark segment of the 163-kilometre North–South Commuter Railway, with JICA supplying the rolling stock and railway systems. Commuter rail widens access to work and services, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Metro Manila Subway Project (Phase 1) (IV)
register.detail: Signed 27 March 2026, Manila · 0.8% a year · 40 years, including 10 years’ grace
register.note: Yen loan for civil works, systems and 240 train cars
register.text: A Japanese loan for civil works, the depot and the Philippines Railway Institute, the railway system and 240 train cars for the Metro Manila Subway. Mass transit widens access to work, schools and hospitals.

register.name: Metro Rail Transit Line 3 Rehabilitation Project (III)
register.detail: Signed 3 March 2026, Manila · 0.80% a year · 40 years, including 10 years’ grace
register.note: Loan of 21,634.83 million yen
register.text: A Japanese loan for the rehabilitation and maintenance of MRT Line 3 in Metro Manila: rolling stock, track, signalling, power systems and stations, with spare parts and maintenance services. Reliable commuter rail serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Laguna Lakeshore Road Network, Phase 1 Stage 1
register.detail: Loan agreement exchanged 17 January 2025 · Civil works by the Department of Public Works and Highways · Completion anticipated by 2029
register.note: Korea’s loan for the first stage of the road network
register.text: A loan from the Export-Import Bank of Korea for the first stage of the Laguna Lakeshore Road Network. The Department of Public Works and Highways slated construction to start in 2025, with completion anticipated by 2029.

register.name: ICTSI container terminals loan
register.detail: Signed, announced 20 May 2026 · Senior unsecured corporate loan · AIIB’s first non-sovereign-backed transaction in the Philippines
register.note: Manila, Batangas and Mindanao container terminals
register.text: AIIB lending to International Container Terminal Services Inc. for port connectivity and a green transition at the Manila International Container Terminal, the South Luzon Container Terminal in Batangas and the Mindanao Container Terminal. Port capacity carries the food and goods trade on which the livelihood standard depends.

register.name: OnePuhunan, senior loan
register.detail: Approved 25 February 2026 · Signed 12 March 2026 · Invested 20 April 2026 · Three years · Up to $40 million more to be mobilized
register.note: On-lending to women microentrepreneurs in rural areas
register.text: An IFC loan to a microfinance institution for on-lending to women-owned or women-led microenterprises in rural Philippines, within a facility of up to $60 million. It finances the livelihood standard directly.

register.name: Fuse Financing (GCash), small business loan
register.detail: Signed 6 February 2026 · Lending arm of the GCash e-wallet · 60% for women-owned businesses
register.note: Digital credit for micro, small and medium enterprises
register.text: An ADB loan to Fuse Financing Inc., the lending arm of GCash, the Philippines’ largest e-wallet provider, to widen credit for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. Fuse will allocate 60% of the proceeds to women-owned businesses, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Maynilad Water Services, IPO cornerstone investment
register.detail: 7 November 2025 · In peso equivalent · $100 million from ADB’s ordinary capital and $45 million from LEAP 2 · One of two lead cornerstone investors
register.note: Metro Manila’s West Zone and parts of Cavite, about 10.5 million people
register.text: ADB’s equity investment in Maynilad’s initial public offering on the Philippine Stock Exchange, to expand and modernise water and wastewater infrastructure: treatment capacity, lower water losses, pipelines and sewer lines. It serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Maynilad Water Services, IPO cornerstone investment
register.detail: 7 November 2025 · Cornerstone investor in the initial public offering
register.note: The largest water concession in the Philippines and Southeast Asia
register.text: IFC’s equity investment in Maynilad’s initial public offering. The proceeds fund Maynilad’s capital expenditure, including wider wastewater coverage, which serves the water and shelter standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 56 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy street in Manila with jeepneys

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: A turquoise lagoon among limestone cliffs in El Nido, Palawan

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A geothermal power plant in the hills of the Philippines

items.name: Maynilad Water Services
items.text: The operator of the largest water concession in the Philippines and Southeast Asia, serving Metro Manila’s West Zone and parts of Cavite, an estimated 10.5 million people. ADB ($145 million) and IFC ($100 million) were cornerstone investors in its initial public offering in November 2025.

items.name: Lhoopa
items.text: Acquires, renovates, builds and sells affordable homes, mainly to middle-income workers such as drivers and teachers, at an average price of Php 850,000 (about $15,000). ADB signed a loan of up to $20 million in March 2024 to help it deliver more affordable housing.

items.name: ACEN Corporation
items.text: An energy company of the Ayala group. In December 2023 ADB and ACEN signed a sustainability-linked loan of up to Php5.5 billion (about $100 million) for solar generation of at least 450 gigawatt-hours a year, replacing power from divested coal plants.

items.name: PHINMA Education
items.text: Owns and operates seven schools across the Philippines for underserved youth. In February 2020 Kaizenvest, FMO and ADB joined a ₱1.875 billion partnership to fund the acquisition and operation of more schools.

items.name: AC Health
items.text: Runs Generika drugstores, Healthway clinics and QualiMed hospitals. In November 2021 IFC invested $100 million in a 10-year social bond of the Ayala group that refinanced a new cancer hospital and the expansion of AC Health’s clinics.

items.name: OnePuhunan
items.text: A microfinance institution lending to women microentrepreneurs in rural areas. IFC invested a three-year loan of $20 million in April 2026, within a facility of up to $60 million.
